Service Diagram (fleet map)

An interactive network diagram of the fleet built from SATOM's cache — Internet → published services (VIP:port) → appliance → server pools → back-end servers — with search, filters, a grouped list, device cards and per-policy detail.

👤 ForViewerOperatorAdministrator
🔑 Permissionsmonitoring.view operations.apply appliances.apply
📍 WhereOperations → Service Diagram (every ADOM); Global home → Global sections → Service Diagram (URL /architecture/)

What is it?#

The Service Diagram draws how the fleet is wired: from the Internet to each published service (VIP and port, with a lock for HTTPS), into the appliance, through its server pools to the back-end servers. Everything comes from SATOM's cache of the device configuration, so the map opens instantly and works with appliances powered off.

To draw a network path yourself (firewalls, segments, VLANs) and read it live from the FortiGates, use Operations → Architecture instead. See Architecture (drawn network diagrams). For the architecture of SATOM itself, see Architecture (technical).

ℹ️Note

Changed in 3.1.0: this page was called Fleet → Architecture until 3.1.0. Its URL is still /architecture/. The name Architecture now belongs to the new drawing page at /net-architecture/.

What does it do?#

  • Map view: devices start collapsed; click one to unfold its topology. Expand all, Collapse, Fit, zoom in/out.
  • List view: devices grouped Zone → Line → Department.
  • Search (device / policy / VIP / WAF / pool / backend ip:port) switches to a focused view showing only the matching paths.
  • Filters (saved per user): Zone, Line, Dept, Kind, Firmware (shown when there is more than one value), and Data (cached / no data), Proto (HTTPS / HTTP), WAF (protected / no WAF), Policy (enabled / disabled).
  • Device card: identity, datasheet (PDF) if uploaded, and Interfaces (port, role, state, address, connected to, notes) merged from the harvest, operator documentation and cached MAC addresses. Fetch MAC addresses (users who can change configuration) reads them over the read-only CLI. Enter device selects the device and opens its ADOM; Open full detail opens the appliance page.
  • Policy detail: everything cached about one server policy with Configure links into the live object editors (virtual server, pool, health check, web protection profile, custom services, VIPs, content routing) and Open policy configuration.
  • The same picker appears in the device-switch dialog of the top bar.

The legend explains the symbols: published service (VIP:port), HTTPS / TLS service, FortiWeb appliance, server pool, back-end servers, traffic path (animated = enabled), disabled policy, WAF profile attached.

Requirements#

  • Appliances registered, ideally with Zone, Line and Department set on the appliance record (used for grouping and filters).
  • A harvest of the devices (device_sync or a rediscovery). Service topology is drawn for FortiWeb server policies found in the cache; a device without cached policies shows as no data.

Permissions#

🔑Permission

Requires the legacy view gate, which any read permission grants (for example monitoring.view); all system profiles have it. Devices are limited to those visible in the current ADOM. Fetch MAC addresses logs in to the appliance over SSH and updates the stored interface inventory, so it needs the legacy config_write gate (e.g. operations.apply or appliances.apply) — the same as the Device health hardware scan. Without it the button is hidden and the endpoint answers 403. The Configure links lead to editors that have their own permission checks.

ℹ️Note

Changed in 2.11.0: this page (then called Architecture) now requires a read permission instead of sign-in alone; Fetch MAC addresses requires config_write and every run is recorded in the audit log.

How to use#

Find where a backend is used#

  1. Open Operations → Service Diagram.
  2. Type 198.51.100.20:8080 in the search box. The map shows only the zones, devices and policies that lead to that backend.
  3. Click a policy node to open its detail, then Open policy configuration.

Filter the map#

Use the filter pills above the map (multi-select). The selection is saved for your user and restored next time. The clear button removes all filters.

Fetch MAC addresses#

  1. Click a device to open its card.
  2. Under Interfaces, click Fetch MAC addresses (shown only with config_write; it reads Refresh MAC addresses once addresses have been fetched). SATOM logs in over SSH, reads the addresses with read-only commands and refreshes the table.

Switch the working device#

Click a device → Enter device. SATOM makes it the current device and opens the right ADOM (FortiWeb devices land on the Server Policy workspace; FortiADC, FortiAnalyzer and FortiAuthenticator devices on their own ADOM home).

Configuration#

Nothing to configure on the page. Grouping fields (Zone, Line, Department) are edited on the appliance — see Appliances. Filter choices are stored per user automatically.

Example#

🧪Example — Which services in zone DMZ have no WAF?

Filter Zone = DMZ, WAF = no WAF, Policy = enabled, then Expand all. Every remaining policy is an enabled published service without a protection profile.

Result#

Viewing changes nothing. Enter device changes your session's current device. Fetch MAC addresses stores the addresses in SATOM's cache and writes an audit entry architecture.fetch_macs with the outcome (success, address count or error).

Troubleshooting#

"No appliances configured"#

Add appliances and assign Zone / Line / Department in Appliances.

A device shows no services#

Its cache holds no server policies yet (or it is not a FortiWeb). Run a rediscovery or wait for device_sync.

"This policy is not in the device cache yet — run a sync or deep capture first."#

The policy detail needs the cached policy. Run a sync.

"No interfaces in the cache for this device."#

Run a device sync, or document ports on the appliance.

"Fetch MAC addresses" is missing from the device card#

Your profile does not hold config_write. Ask a user who can change configuration, or an administrator, to run it.

Fetch MAC addresses fails#

The read-only SSH session could not be opened or the command failed (the error is shown). Check SSH credentials on the appliance.

Advanced#

Advanced Data sources
  • Topology: the cached server policies (deep layer if present, else the config layer), their VIPs, pools and backends; service ports from custom services (HTTP = 80, HTTPS = 443 otherwise).
  • The map never calls an appliance; only Fetch MAC addresses does.
  • Saved filters live in the user's settings (architecture_filters).
